doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Mike Longo's Kundalini anecdote about Dizzy
summary: Rowe relays Longo's story of Dizzy's answer about where his music came from; Berroa never discussed the theory.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: That’s a great analogy. I was able to do an interview with Mike Longo and he told me this little anecdote about Dizzy from the film “A Night in Havana.”

And I’m going to sort of read a quote from his interview here. A woman asked him, “Where does your music come from.” And he said, “Do you really want to know?” And she said well yes. You know what he said? He said “my asshole.”

So then Mike went on to say that this actually has a name, a Kundalini Energy, like an ultimate life force, that there’s actually a philosophy about this energy that’s stored in the bass of your spine and if you operate correctly it will go to your head and allow you to do certain things.
So I wonder if you had a comment on that?

No. I don’t know because we never talked about that. I remember him saying when the student asked him what was the first thing, how he was able to play those high notes, he used to say the first thing that you have to do is you have to tighten your asshole. That was the first thing that he would say. So that answer that he gave to that lady in Cuba, we never talked about that theory. We never talked about it.
